headline: House Prosecutors Say They Will Drop the Bribery Article in Sara Duterte Impeachment Trial
seoTitle: Prosecutors to Drop Bribery Article in Duterte Trial
seoDescription: House prosecutors say they will drop Article 3, the bribery allegation, in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial. A formal manifestation was expected on October 5.
deck: Prosecutors said they would formalize the decision before the Senate impeachment court on Monday. Vice President Sara Duterte has not been convicted of anything.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: House prosecutors said they will no longer pursue Article 3 of the impeachment complaint against Vice President Sara Duterte, the allegation that she bribed Department of Education officials to circumvent procurement rules while she was education secretary. Rep. Joel Chua confirmed the plan on Sunday, October 4. Lead prosecutor Rep. Gerville Luistro said on Monday, October 5, that the panel would present a formal manifestation of its position before the Senate impeachment court that day.

By Monday afternoon, no independent report had confirmed that the manifestation was already on the Senate record. Chua said the reason was not weakness in the case and that the evidence presented was already sufficient.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said dropping the charge could leave Filipinos without "the whole truth" but that the decision belongs to the prosecution. Luistro said the panel remains committed to completing its case without unnecessary delay and pointed to evidence already before the court on confidential funds and grave threats, with presentation on unexplained wealth ongoing.

Separately, the Supreme Court en banc earlier dismissed three petitions challenging the Senate impeachment court's September 23 ruling on how many votes are needed to convict. Reporting on September 30 and October 1 said the Court cited lack of legal standing and prematurity and did not grant a temporary restraining order. FMB News has not seen a Supreme Court release confirming the date of the resolution itself.

Under the impeachment court's September 23 approach, only senator-judges "legally and factually capable" of taking part are counted. With 20 active senator-judges, reports put the conviction threshold at 14 votes and acquittal at seven. That threshold remains in place after the petitions were dismissed.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Dropping Article 3 leaves fewer allegations for the Senate to decide. Prosecutors have said they aim to finish presenting evidence by mid-October, when the chamber is also expected to prioritise the 2027 budget.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next thing to confirm is whether the manifestation on Article 3 appears in the Senate record.
